newsitem.title: CANADA: Airline '96 op profit at 4.3 pct of revenues - ICAO.
newsitem.headline: Airline '96 op profit at 4.3 pct of revenues - ICAO.

text.p: Operating profit for the world's scheduled airlines dropped to 4.3 percent of revenues in 1996 from 5.1 percent in 1995, the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) said (on) Wednesday.

Operating revenues of scheduled airlines for ICAO's 185 contracting states, excluding the Commonwealth of Independent States, are tentatively estimated at US$281.5 billion in 1996, versus operating expenses of US$269.5 billion, ICAO said.
Operating revenues rose by 5 percent in 1996, compared with a six percent increase in expenses and eight percent rise in traffic, the United Nations specialized agency said.
Despite the weaker profit margin, world airlines reported an operating profit in 1996 for the fourth year in a row.

Operating revenues per tonne-kilometre performed fell to an estimated 85.4 U.S. cents in 1996 from 87.3 U.S. cents in 1995, while operating expenses per tonne-kilometre performed decreased to an estimated 81.8 U.S. cents from 82.9 U.S. cents.

The smaller operating profit in 1996 reflects cost pressures, notably from higher aviation fuel prices, a higher value of the U.S. dollar in relation to other world currencies and a levelling in the average load factor despite strong traffic growth.

The net result for 1996 -- after non-operating expenses such as interest and subsidies -- and income taxes, is expected to be better than in 1995 because of lower interest rates, improved airline balance sheets and because airlines spent less money spent in 1996 on restructuring.
